events.title: Elijah swears a drought before Ahab
events.narrative_summary: Elijah the Tishbite appears without introduction and swears by YHWH that there will be neither dew nor rain except by his word.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The text gives no regnal year. The oath is placed within Ahab's 22-year reign (1 Kgs 16:29), centred 11 years after accession with a ±9-year margin. This is a fixture placement, not a scholarly claim.
events.ancient_year_marker: During the reign of Ahab (year unstated)

entities.etymology_meaning: "My God is YHWH" (Eli + Yahu): the name is itself the thesis of the Carmel contest.
entities.summary_bio: Prophet from Tishbe in Gilead who confronts Ahab and Jezebel over the worship of Baal. He announces a drought, defeats the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, flees to Horeb, and appoints Elisha as his successor.

Seventh king of the northern kingdom of Israel and son of Omri. He married the Phoenician princess Jezebel and sponsored Baal worship in Samaria. Assyrian records name him as a major military power at the battle of Qarqar.

aliases: God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel
entities.etymology_meaning: The divine name, usually linked to the verb "to be" (Exod 3:14). Traditionally not pronounced; English versions render it "the LORD".
entities.summary_bio: The God of Israel, whose claim to send rain and fire is tested against Baal's on Mount Carmel.
